newsitem.title: USA: NY counties push Pataki to get welfare bonus-paper.
newsitem.headline: NY counties push Pataki to get welfare bonus-paper.

text.p: Some counties in New York State are pressing Gov. George Pataki to give them more of a $450 million windfall expected under the first year of the new federal welfare rules, the Albany Times Union said Wednesday.

Albany County Executive Michael Breslin told the paper his locality needs the cash to help offset $3 million in spending caps and cuts created by the nw state welfare program. He said that would translate into a seven percent property tax hike next year.

New York State gets the windfall because the $2.36 billion block grant it expects to get in 1996-1997 is based on how many people collected benefits in 1995, a total that has fallen this year. But the paper said the Pataki Administration wanted to pay back counties based on their 1996 caseloads.
State Social Services Commissioner Brian Wing told the paper that counties that are cutting back are not being penalized because their caseloads are dropping.

And it quoted John Signor, state Budget Division spokesman, as saying that the state should share in the savings because the Pataki Administration's policies, like figner printing, have helped cut caseloads by more than 220,000 since the governor took office.
The paper said Pataki's plan would give $105 million to the state to help close the budget gap and pay for programs like education and Medicaid.
Another $105 million would go to the counties for fiscal relief. And $240 million would be earmarked for welfare.
